# Pending changes (since patch 0016, 2026-11-21)
## 2026-11-21 - The Minoan kit: procedural pieces; daylight in the shade

**Asked:** advice on editing the assets in Blender, then: "I want everything for now to be kept procedural, I can always add static meshes on top of procedural kit bashes - proceed like this".

**Done:**
- **New pieces for the town builder** (CosmosTown.Builder), all made in code, still one mesh and one draw per town, on a worker:
  - smooth-shaded primitives: a lathe (shapes turned round an axis, a slot for each stretch), tubes along a path, round discs out of a wall;
  - Minoan columns on the lathe: a dark stone base, the red shaft wider at the top, the round cushion capital, its square block;
  - horns of consecration that curve up and out (tubes), not boxes;
  - storage jars (pithoi) on the lathe, with a rope band;
  - the palace's frieze: the round ends of its roof beams in a row under the cornice;
  - window frames in timber (sill, lintel, a mullion), and a timber beam laid in the masonry each storey.
- **Surfaces made in the shader** (building.gdshader), on each face's own plane:
  - cut stone in courses of ashlar blocks, the joints darker, each block its own tone (the stone; in a dungeon the walls too; a cave stays rough rock);
  - the frescoes' running spirals between red borders (each band's base height rides in the vertex colour);
  - wood grain.
- **Daylight in the shade:** on a world with air, by day, the ambient light is the sky's (it was a dim space grey everywhere, so shaded walls and slopes went navy-black); it fades as you climb out of the air or the sun sets.

**Numbers:** a palace column 36 -> ~200 triangles (a city has ~20); a jar 36 -> ~140 (~100 a city); the palace frieze ~700 beam ends. Frame rate not measured: another game was using the GPU (92%) and 7 CPU cores - to measure on a quiet machine.

**Tests:** all pass; doc shots retaken (towns, the ground, the dungeons).

**Files:** scripts/world/life/cosmos_town.gd (lathe, tube, disc, quad_n, column, horns, _jar, _beam_ends, windows, the timber beams, the "ashlar" parameter), shaders/world/building.gdshader, scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd (AMBIENT_SKY).

## 2026-11-21 - Mining in 3D

**Asked:** "proceed ... and any other pending tasks" (the 2D game's systems not yet in 3D: mining first).

**Done:**
- **Mining asteroids** (CosmosMining; the rules are the 2D game's - Mining): fire with your sights on an asteroid within 1.5 km and the ship cuts it with its red mining beam instead of its guns (the rock becomes your target; T on one does too).
  - **The scan:** a targeted rock within 3 km is scanned in two seconds - its minerals, and its veins marked on the rock as it tumbles. Unscanned, a rock gives only rubble.
  - **Cutting:** the beam cuts the vein nearest your sights; its heat on a bar with the green cutting band (slow below, full speed in it with resonance building, strained above, fractured at the top - a share lost as rubble); let go and it cools; harder minerals heat faster. The mining speed and ore yield upgrades count.
  - **Fragments** go into the hold until it's full (a refinery makes minerals of them); a rock shrinks as it's mined and is gone mined out - kept so in the save (CosmosGame.extra "mined": each rock's veins, ore, scan).
  - **The HUD:** the rock's veins on it (the one being cut ringed), the readout over the toolbar - the scan, the three main minerals, the vein's heat and band, resonance, what you've cut.
- **The rocks' tumble by a known clock:** the rock shader turned each rock by the shader's own time, which a script can't read; now by a `clock` the field sets each frame, so CosmosRocks knows where every point of a rock's surface is (its mesh's noise kept) - the veins sit on the rock as it turns. Each field is iron, titanium or platinum.
- **Fragments in the hold:** PlayerData.held_items() left mining fragments out (the inventory and the refinery never listed them) - they're listed now.
- **Fixes:** an error when an NPC ship's engine glows were rebuilt; arriving at a system's origin (nothing to face).

**Numbers:** a field 320 rocks, 4-74 m, 12 ore a metre of radius (48-890 a rock), 2-5 veins; the beam 1.5 km, the scan 3 km / 2 s.

**Tests:** test_cosmos.test_mining_an_asteroid (T on a rock, the scan, cutting in pulses - fragments, heat into the band, the rock shrinking, kept in the save - a fracture, mined out and gone). Doc shot space3d_mining (new), the guide's "Mining asteroids".

**Files:** scripts/world/space/cosmos_mining.gd (new), cosmos_rocks.gd (rewritten: clock, state, surface_at, vein_at, mined, ray), shaders/world/rock.gdshader, scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd (mining, pick_target, bodies, radius_of), scripts/world/player/cosmos_ship.gd (the beam before the guns), cosmos_hud.gd (_draw_mining), scripts/sim/player_data.gd, cosmos_planet.gd / cosmos_warm.gd (the rock mesh's new return), cosmos_npc_ship.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd, tests/doc_shots.gd, data/docs/game.md, data/docs/shots.json.

## 2026-11-21 - Frame rate near the ground: the quadtree visited in slices

**Asked:** the pending frame-rate work (the 600 FPS bar; the slowest frames low over a planet).

**Done:**
- **The visit in slices:** a planet's quadtree visit (split, merge, show, hide) cost ~1.5 ms of script near the ground and ran whole in one frame, 8-30 times a second - at 600 FPS one frame in twenty, exactly the slow 5%. Now a visit runs from a list, 0.3 ms a frame (VISIT_BUDGET_US), and goes on in the next frames till it's done (CosmosPlanet.update_lod / visiting(); Cosmos keeps a visit begun going).
- **The horizon test without arccosines:** each patch's "beyond the horizon?" is a dot product against a cosine worked out once a visit for each level.
- **The boulders near the ship and the camera:** the two callers asking every frame reuse their last answer for 0.1 s while they've moved little (found with a 6 m margin).
- Tried and dropped: a smaller budget for turning finished patches into meshes (no gain).

**Numbers (fps_test.py 3d, quiet machine):** low over the sea 527 -> ~600 FPS, p95 4.0 -> 2.7-2.9 ms, 1% low 137 -> 245-275; on foot 604 -> ~700, p95 2.4 -> 1.9-2.0 ms; the others as before (town ~535, pirate camp ~575 - next). A visit measured: 1.55 ms median. Baseline saved.

**Files:** scripts/world/space/cosmos_planet.gd (update_lod, _begin_visit, visiting, _visit, _in_sight, rocks_near's cache), scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd (_update_lod; the callers' keys), tests/fps_baseline.json; data/docs/shots.json (the on-foot shot's eagle note dropped - the eagle's never in the same place).

## 2026-11-21 - Landing on pads: a landing display, R / F thrusters, a throttle with a detent; faster pulse bolts

Asked: "make a specialised hud for when landing on a landing pad on a station so it is easy to align the
ship correctly, r should raise the ship and f should lower it, backward thrust should be a negative value and
also it should much easier to snap to zero thrust"; then "pulse lazer bullets should be a lot faster, its very
hard to hit space pirates currently".

Done:
- **The landing display** (CosmosHud._draw_landing): within 600 m of your pad, a panel on the right - the
  scope (the pad's square from above, your ship in the middle nose up, range rings 30 / 60 / 120 / 250 /
  600 m picked to fit, an arrow at the rim when the pad's beyond it, the drift line = 2 s of your motion over
  the deck), the height tape (gear over the deck, its scale 25 - 600 m, the climb / sink rate signed), the
  level bubble (inside the inner ring = within the 32° the touchdown allows), speed, the thrust signed (THR /
  LIFT / SIDE in %), a status (OFF THE PAD / OVER THE PAD / TOUCHDOWN) and what still stops a touchdown
  ("Over the square first", "Level the ship", "Slower than 12 m/s", "Down: F"). In the view: the pad's
  square outlined (green when you're over it) and a dashed line dropped from the ship to the deck under it
  (the ship hides the pad from the camera behind it).
- **R / F thrusters up / down** (Keybinds "up" = R + Space, "down" = F + Ctrl). F used to ask for a pad:
  now **L near a station asks for a pad** (again: cancels) - L lands near planets, docks near stations; the
  "dock" action keeps no key (the touch button still uses it). Prompts read the key from Keybinds.
- **The throttle**: negative = backward thrust, shown signed ("+45%" / "-12%") by the bar, a tick at zero;
  a **detent at zero** - W / S stop at 0 on the way through (let go and press again to go on), and a throttle
  left within 6% of zero snaps to it (CosmosShip._set_throttle, REVERSE 0.25).
- **Pulse bolts** (yours in space): 2600 m/s (was 900) **plus your ship's velocity** (they weren't carried
  on it - chasing a raider at 180 m/s they closed at only 720 m/s, and the lead marker assumed they were);
  1.5 s life (3.9 km); hits 3 m more forgiving (PULSE_SLACK). The lead (Cosmos.ship_aim) uses the new speed.
  Raiders' bolts unchanged (900 m/s).
- Guide (game.md: flying, landing and docking, stations) and tutorial updated; the space3d_pad shot retaken
  with new notes.

Files: scripts/world/player/cosmos_hud.gd, cosmos_ship.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, cosmos_bolt.gd,
scripts/core/keybinds.gd, data/docs/game.md, tutorial.md, shots.json, shots/space3d_pad.jpg.

## 2026-11-21 - Mining carves asteroids; mining deposits on foot

Asked: "mining should actually carve the terrain of an asteroid, also planet surface has mining".

Done:
- **Carved asteroids** (CosmosRocks.carve, _carve_step, _fine_arrays, _dent): a rock's first cut gives it a
  mesh of its own - a finer sphere (48 x 24 segments, ~1,200 vertices; the shared ones 20 x 10) pushed out by
  the same noise, built on a worker (at most every 0.15 s, swapped in when done) and drawn as a multimesh of
  one with the same tumble; its instance in the shared multimesh hidden. Craters are bowls (centre in the
  rock's unit space, radius, depth, rough by a noise): **each vein becomes a pit** that deepens (to 0.54 of
  the radius) and widens with the square root of the share cut (so it shows from the first cuts),
  **fractures** blow a rough crater beside it, **bulk hacking** leaves craters where the beam strikes (merged
  when close; at most 48 a rock). The vein's mark (surface_at / vein_at) sits at the pit's bottom; a carved
  rock barely shrinks (to 0.82 of its size: the pits show what's gone). Craters kept in the save
  ("mined" -> "craters") and rebuilt on arrival.
- **Mining on foot** (new CosmosDeposits, shaders/world/deposit.gdshader): round you on a planet, deposits
  of its minerals - **crystal clusters** (ice, salt, sulphur, obsidian, orichalcum: 9 hexagonal prisms with
  pointed tips on a stub of rock) and **ore boulders** (two noise lumps, the metal in veins through the
  rock: iron, copper, tin, silver, gold, cobalt, titanium, platinum). Which by the kind of world (MIX:
  glacier, inferno, ocean, alien, barren, moon). One a 40 m grid cell at most (55%, its ground point in its
  cell), seeded - the same ones in the same places every visit - found on a worker within 160 m as you walk
  (looked over every 18 m, paced by time). Two shared meshes, one material, the minerals as instance
  uniforms (tint, metal, glow, heat). **Fire** with your sights on one within 30 m: a mining beam from your
  hand cuts it instead of the rifle - 3 units a second straight into your pack as the mineral (no
  refining); it shrinks (0.3 + 0.7 sqrt(left)), mined out it breaks up and is gone for good
  (CosmosGame.extra "dug"). The beam heats (0.22/s x hardness), at the top **overheats** and stops till
  cooled right down. Solid: you step round them. HUD beside the sights: the deposit and what's left, the
  beam's heat, what you've dug. Warmed at the title (CosmosWarm._deposit).
- Tests: test_mining_an_asteroid (carved: pit, mesh, mark at the bottom, saved), test_mining_deposits_on_foot
  (found, seeded, cut, pack, heat, overheat, cool, mined out, saved). Guide: "Mining on foot" section, the
  asteroid section on carving; new shot space3d_dig; space3d_mining shows a half-dug pit; space3d_fight's
  raider held still so its notes keep pointing at it.

scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, cosmos_hud.gd, scripts/world/models/cosmos_warm.gd,

## 2026-11-21 - Digging: voxel ground where you carve

Asked: "add digging" (to mining on foot), then "make the terrain voxel based".

Done:
- **The terrain digger** (CosmosDeposits; V switches the rifle for it, Keybinds "tool"): fire and the beam
  carves a sphere (2 m) out of the ground where the sights meet it (a march through the density, 0.6 m steps
  then halved to ~1 cm), every 0.15 s, its middle 0.6 r back along the beam - held on one spot it bores in
  along it (down into a pit, into a hillside as a tunnel; ~0.8 m a cut), swept it cuts a trench. Not in a
  town; no deeper than 30 m; heats the beam (0.13/s). HUD: "TERRAIN DIGGER" and bracket sights.
- **Carves** (PlanetShape): the ground is solid below the heightfield except inside the carves -
  `density(p)` (> 0 air, < 0 solid) = the heightfield's, the carves cut out (max). Each carve stored as its
  direction (64-bit: in 32 the dot of two near directions loses ~1 m on a 3 km planet), radius, its middle's
  height; a hash of 16 m cells for the main thread's lookups, snapshots for the workers; kept per planet in
  the save (CosmosGame.extra "digs", [x, y, z, r, top]). `floor_below` (down to the first solid - a pit's,
  a tunnel's floor; up out of the rock), `push_out` (along the density's slope to air).
- **Voxels** (new CosmosVoxels, a child of the planet): 8 m chunks of 0.5 m voxels (16^3, sampled with a
  voxel's border for the seams) on a grid fixed to the planet; the heights from a grid of their own on the
  chunk's tangent plane (bilinear: ~1,100 height samples a chunk instead of ~6,900); meshed by **surface
  nets** (a vertex per crossed cell at the mean of its edge crossings, normals from the density's slope, a
  quad per crossed edge the chunk owns), only the quads within 0.45 m of a carve kept - the rest is the
  heightfield's. Built on workers (3 at once, nearest first; again when a carve touches them), made for the
  carves within 220 m, dropped beyond 320 m. Drawn with the planet's terrain material.
- **The heightfield not drawn inside the carves** (terrain.gdshader: `cuts[128]` - the carves nearest you,
  0.3 m in - `cut_n`, and an instance `cut_on` on the patches with carves near them, so only those loop):
  the voxels' surface shows there, overlapping its rim. Patches near a carve rebuilt (their plants and
  boulders in it go: dug_here). Shadows too (the same discard): the sun into a pit, a cave dark.
- **On foot in dug ground**: the walker's floor from the density (into pits, along tunnels), its knees and
  head pushed out of the walls; the camera kept out of the walls (keep_above_ground: push_out; camera_clear:
  a march to the first solid).
- Tests: test_digging_the_ground (digger out, ~20 cuts bore down > 4 m, air where it was solid, a cave
  under solid ground, chunks meshed, the shader told, the walker's floor in the hole, the save carves the
  same, V back to the rifle). Guide: "Digging the ground"; shot space3d_digging.
- Deposits drawn to 110 m only, kept within 130 m (was 160): the pirate camp back to ~560 FPS, the town ~540
  (a busy machine had shown 433 / 498); every scenario within its baseline.

Files: scripts/world/space/planet_shape.gd, cosmos_planet.gd, cosmos_voxels.gd (new), cosmos_deposits.gd,
cosmos.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, cosmos_hud.gd, scripts/core/keybinds.gd,
shaders/world/terrain.gdshader, tests/test_cosmos.gd, tests/doc_shots.gd, data/docs/game.md, shots.json,
shots/space3d_digging.jpg (new).

## 2026-11-21 - The target's window

Asked: "when i lock on a target i want on the left up corner a viewport to appear that shows the target
with its stats - a ship or npc: health, shield, weapons, speed; a stellar body: size, orbit, type".

Done:
- **CosmosTargetView** (new, the HUD layer): under the ship's gauge, top left (where the one-line
  "Target:" readout and its two bars were - gone from CosmosHud). A SubViewport 380 x 210 on the same
  world, its own camera circling the target (0.22 rad/s), standing back so it fills ~60% of the view, from
  its star's lit side; a ship from its own up, a gate through its ring, the star from above the planets'
  plane, a town from its sky. Rendered 30 times a second (UPDATE_ONCE on a timer), only while there's a
  target; no lamp shadows in it; one frame drawn under the loading veil (its buffers made then).

  - stations: state bar, kind (economy), flag, sells, buys, free pads;
  - gates: where to, who rules there, its star, the ring's size; towns, bio-signatures, asteroids (ore

## 2026-11-22 - Station pads: shafts and shutters

Asked: "now do the same for the landing doors on the landing pad of a station" (the pad's lift sank the
ship straight into the solid platform - it seemed to vanish into it).

Done:
- **Platforms with shafts** (CosmosStation._platform, both station builders): a platform's deck is a frame
  of parts round a square hole a pad, under each hole a shaft down to the lift's depth (Cosmos.LIFT_DEPTH +
  8 m): dark walls, three rows of lamps down them, a floor. The pad's deck is the lift. Its rim lights moved
  out onto the frame (they stay at the top as the deck goes down).
- **Shutters** (CosmosStation._pad, _shutters, set_hatch): each pad's shaft is closed by telescoping slats -
  stacked on the platform beside the pad when open (two a side for the small pads, five for the big), they
  slide out over the hole one under another, the far ones first, and settle side by side to meet in the
  middle; the leading slat's edge lit. All a station's slats are instances of one mesh (two draws: slats,
  edges), placed by set_hatch.
- **Docking** (Cosmos._docking): the lift takes you down the lit shaft; once you're below the rim the
  shutters slide shut over you (HATCH_TIME 1.8 s), then the dark - the hangar. **Undocking**: light, the
  shutters slide open over you, the lift brings you up, take-off.
- The Minoan bay's four warm lamps taken out again (they cost the hangar ~190 FPS): its cream wall panels
  light it enough. Shot space3d_hangar: the walker runs a few metres off the pad first (the camera clear of
  the bigger ship's tail); space3d_pad retaken.
- Frame rate: every scenario within its baseline (a busy machine: Brave at 136%).
